transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Aurora - Head of ML), Tom (Platform), Priya (Product)
Links shared: sheet://pilot_metrics_v2.xlsx, drive://aurora/poc/logs (note: shared after call), slide deck: https://redwood.com/pilot-playbook (AE deck)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh we'll try to keep this to 40 minutes. Quick recap: saw a spike in false positives in the last 48 hours on the quantized deploy, so wanted to triage and decide next steps. Diego is on to walk through the traces.

[00:22] Diego (Redwood SE): yeah hi all, hi lena, tom — so I pulled the sampling from your test harness, the 1k example set from last week. The pattern I'm seeing, and this is preliminary, is twofold: first warmup KV cache behavior where cold requests hit higher latency and slightly different decoding paths, and second some subtle tokenization drift when using the 4-bit quant profile we shipped.

[00:45] Lena (Aurora): okay so, are those two things related? because we only saw the scoring delta on specific prompts that used nested codeblocks and some long prefixed context, so wondered if it's the prefix trimming you mentioned before.

[01:05] Diego (Redwood SE): yup, kind of related. The prefix/KV caching means when the model sees an identical prefix it reuses kv, but with the batching and the quant kernels we've tuned, there are edge cases where the attention kernel selection differs when sequence lengths vary — um, that can produce slightly different logits around boundary tokens. So in most cases it's fine but with your scoring threshold it's pushing some borderline examples over.

[01:34] Tom (Aurora): just to interject — when you say "quant kernels differ" are we talking about model architecture change or runtime kernel selection? because we can't change the model weights.

[01:44] Diego (Redwood SE): runtime kernel selection only, so weights identical. It's about the optimized path we take for perf on A100 vs 4-bit path on our dedicated nodes; on some long sequences we pick a different matmul kernel and the FP-to-int rounding behavior differs slightly. Not a model drift, more of a numeric path difference.

[02:10] Priya (Aurora): that actually explains why product saw more false positives in the morning spikes — traffic pattern changed and batch sizes increased.

[02:19] Maya (Redwood AE): yeah and that ties into the latency vs cost tradeoff — where batching gives better cost but maybe increases those boundary artifacts. Quick qualification: are you folks on a hosted plan or dedicated for this pilot?

[02:34] Lena (Aurora): currently on hosted with the quantized variant. We're evaluating dedicated if it buys stability and consistent kernels, and we've seen some doc notes about dedicated offers pinning kernel/compilation profiles. But we'd like to confirm.

[02:50] Diego (Redwood SE): correct, dedicated lets us pin the compilation profile and the kernel set, you get consistent execution and we can disable automatic kernel fallback that causes the small numeric differences. It also gives you more control on KV cache sizing and warmup policies.

[03:08] Speaker 1 (Aurora): (murmur) ok

[03:12] Lena (Aurora): quick sec — security question: if we move to dedicated, what's the data residency and KMS behavior? We need to ensure SSO and KMS integration for secrets.

[03:22] Maya (Redwood AE): good call — dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering in the private deployment option; we also have SOC2 Type II and can provide audit logs. I'll attach the SOC doc after the call.

[03:36] Tom (Aurora): is SAML single-sign on covered? we need SCIM provisioning ideally.

[03:40] Diego (Redwood SE): SAML/SSO, SCIM, RBAC all supported; on private deployments you get more fine-grained network controls. There's a short checklist in the security deck, I'll point you to it.

[03:56] Lena (Aurora): thanks. Back to the regression — can you show a concrete example of the prompt that flipped?

[04:05] Diego (Redwood SE): yep, pulled two contrasting samples — prompt A (good) and prompt B (failed). I'll read them: Prompt B has a long context with system note plus two code fences. With the quant path, token probabilities around the closing fence drop and then the reranker bumps it into a different label.

[04:30] Priya (Aurora): this is the one where the UI flagged escalation when it shouldn't have — so product calls that a false positive.

[04:36] Diego (Redwood SE): exactly. So mitigation options: 1) adjust scoring thresholds for those prompt families; 2) change batching/warmup config to ensure KV cache is hot for those requests; 3) move to dedicated and pin kernel set; 4) try alternate quant recipe we haven't shipped to hosted yet (more conservative quant) — each has tradeoffs on cost/latency.

[05:02] Lena (Aurora): what's the expected delta if we tweak thresholds? we worry about increasing false negatives.

[05:10] Diego (Redwood SE): reasonable question — based on the sample, a +0.04 threshold bump reduces false positives by ~72% but increases false negatives marginally — maybe 5% on different test slice; we'd want to run the full labeled set.

[05:27] Maya (Redwood AE): maybe a short A/B: keep hosted as control and route 10% to dedicated or to the alternate quant path, run for 48 hours and compare. That way product can see real user signal.

[05:41] Tom (Aurora): cost concerns — dedicated seems pricey, any burst options?

[05:46] Maya (Redwood AE): yes we have a burst policy for dedicated where you reserve baseline capacity and burst to hosted for peaks — that gives cost smoothing. I'll send a sample pricing matrix.

[06:00] Lena (Aurora): curious — Diego, you mentioned KV warmup policy — is there a config we can tune on our end or is that runtime?

[06:09] Diego (Redwood SE): there's a few knobs: you can pre-warm with synthetic traffic, set a min_keepalive TTL for cache entries, or we can enable proactive prefetch for known prefixes. Some of those need dedicated because of memory footprint.

[06:26] Lena (Aurora): hmm ok pre-warm seems doable for critical endpoints.

[06:30] Diego (Redwood SE): also, one other thought — your prompt set has some borderline examples that are long and rare; we recommend a small ensemble reranker or a fallback to a higher-precision model on those cases. That adds latency on a small fraction but reduces FP.

[06:46] Priya (Aurora): fallback sounds interesting — what does that look like in the console?

[06:50] Diego (Redwood SE): in Console you can set route rules: if score between X and Y then call higher-precision model or call function to run additional checks. We can demo that — it’s pretty standard.

[07:05] Lena (Aurora): ok let's talk data collection — we've uploaded the failing examples to the shared sheet but I know there were more in Sentry. We'll consolidate and label + expected outcome.

[07:16] Maya (Redwood AE): perfect — recommended format is: id, prompt snippet, actual label, expected label, context size, observed latency. That helps Diego's bisect.

[07:30] Tom (Aurora): about the bisect — how fast can we narrow it to kernel vs quant recipe vs prompt artifact?

[07:36] Diego (Redwood SE): usually 48–72 hours if we have labeled failing prompts and the logs. Steps: reproduce on a controlled runner, toggle quant recipes, toggle kernel pinning, adjust batching. If we can't repro locally, we escalate to a live-run with tracing flags enabled.

[07:58] Priya (Aurora): what flags — is that intrusive?

[08:01] Diego (Redwood SE): just additional tracing for internal decisions (kernel selection, seq-len mapping), it increases log verbosity but not user visible. We'll need you to opt-in for that run.

[08:12] Maya (Redwood AE): okay so action plan we talked earlier — Diego runs reproducer and a 24h stress on a dedicated replica with tracing; Lena sends full labels; Maya sends pricing and SOC docs. Anything else?

[08:27] Lena (Aurora): can we also get a chart of token-level latency distribution? our ops team wants to see tails, not just p95.

[08:35] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, we'll include p50/p95/p99 plus token-level latency histograms and KV cache hit-rate.

[08:44] Tom (Aurora): one more: our legal folks asked if Redwood supports bringing-your-own-hsm (BYOHSM) or just cloud KMS?

[08:51] Maya (Redwood AE): we support cloud KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments; I'll attach HSM integration notes.

[08:58] Lena (Aurora): excellent.

[09:02] --- Mid-call troubleshooting (crosstalk, faint interruptions) ---
[12:20] Diego (Redwood SE): I just pushed a quick repro to the shared runner, link in chat. It reproduces one failing sample under quant-4b + batching=32. If you folks can glance and confirm it's the same one you saw.

[12:40] Lena (Aurora): opening, yes that's the one. The UI shows the different label.

[13:01] Maya (Redwood AE): note for product: we also have a small change to the reranker that reduces sensitivity to punctuation noise — that might help your code-fence cases too. We can toggle that server-side for a canary.

[13:18] Priya (Aurora): ok do that, if it's low-risk we'll try a 10% canary.

[13:24] Diego (Redwood SE): low-risk but we'll monitor regressions — will create an A/B test route.

[13:35] Lena (Aurora): one procedural question — if we accept dedicated will there be a lead time to spin up pinned kernels?

[13:43] Diego (Redwood SE): depending on capacity, typical lead time is 3–5 business days to provision and pin; if you need faster we can try a warm-up shared node with same profile but dedicated is ideal.

[14:00] Maya (Redwood AE): pricing again — for pilot sized at ~200k tokens/day, I'll share two scenarios: hosted quant path vs dedicated baseline + burst. You'll see a comparative cost per 1k tokens.

[14:16] Tom (Aurora): please include the cost impact of fallback to higher-precision model for 2% of traffic.

[14:22] Maya (Redwood AE): will do.

[14:30] Diego (Redwood SE): quick technical note: we noticed the tokenizer library had a minor patch between versions that changed some whitespace handling; I don't think you upgraded but if you did, that could explain tiny shifts. 

[14:48] Lena (Aurora): we pinned tokenizer at v1.3.2 but dev did a sandbox with v1.4 last week maybe — I'll double-check.

[15:00] Priya (Aurora): okay so for the immediate mitigations, can we list them and owners?

[15:08] Maya (Redwood AE): yep — Diego will run 24h stress + tracing on dedicated replica; Diego will produce latency histograms and kernel selection logs.

[15:18] Diego (Redwood SE): yes and I'll try the alternate quant recipe in parallel and capture diffs.

[15:24] Lena (Aurora): I'll upload the labeled failing prompts to pilot_metrics_v2.xlsx and flag the ones that are high-risk.

[15:32] Maya (Redwood AE): I'll send pricing, SOC2, and HSM notes; propose times for a fallback drill.

[15:38] Tom (Aurora): can we get the expected delta numbers in the email so legal and infra can review?

[15:43] Maya (Redwood AE): yes I'll include a short bullets doc with expected deltas and costs.

[15:49] --- Closing and recap ---
[15:52] Maya (Redwood AE): recap: Diego 24h repro + alternate quant recipe, include p50/p95/p99 and token histograms — due 11/15. Lena upload labeled set due 11/14. Maya send pricing + SOC + HSM doc due 11/13. We'll schedule fallback drill for 11/18 or 11/19 pending availability.

[16:18] Priya (Aurora): sounds good. One last Q: do we need to open a support ticket for the tracing run or is that part of Diego's work?

[16:26] Diego (Redwood SE): I'll open the internal ticket and tag you — it'll have links to logs and artifacts.

[16:35] Lena (Aurora): thanks everyone, this was useful.

[16:40] Maya (Redwood AE): thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and next steps.

[16:45] (call ends)
